_status: Dev URLs discovered from client/vite.config.ts (server.port 5173, /api proxied to :3010) and server/.env.example (PORT=3010). QA, staging and production hostnames still NEED INPUT.

variables._note: Global variables are for values that are genuinely the SAME in every environment. Anything secret-shaped belongs in environments[<env>].variables so a dev secret can never be carried into staging or production (MUST-46).
variables._absent_uuid_note: A syntactically valid UUID that NO record has, for the negative test cases that assert 404. It cannot come from {{cache:...}} the way MUST-36 asks for a foreign key, because the whole point is that no producer created it — a cached id would exist and the endpoint would answer 200 or 409 instead of the 404 under test. Global rather than per-environment because the nil UUID is absent in every environment by construction, and it is not secret-shaped.
variables._not_a_uuid_note: A deliberately malformed id for the negative cases that assert 400 on a non-UUID path param. Cannot come from {{cache:...}} the way MUST-36 asks, for the same reason as absent_uuid and more so: the whole point is that it is NOT a valid id, so no producer could ever emit it.
variables._absent_saga_run_id_note: A well-formed saga run id that matches NO run, for the lookup negative on GET /api/leadflow/sagas/{run_id}. A run id IS the idempotency key - derived from the business identity - so it is NOT a UUID, which makes {{dynamic:uuid}} the wrong SHAPE as well as banned by MUST-36 in a foreign-key position. Global for the same reason as absent_uuid: no API creates a saga run purely to be missed, so it is absent in every environment by construction, and it is not secret-shaped.
variables._upstream_deal_id_note: The deal half of the closed-won key on POST /api/leadflow/closed-won/start. MUST-36 asks for {{cache:...}} from a producer and there is none to trace to: deals are created in sdk-crm through the SDK gateway, and NO LeadFlow route creates one - grep for a deal-creating endpoint under tests/api_definitions and server/src/routes and there is nothing to depend on. That makes this the last-resort {{var:name}} form the rule allows. The case it appears in asserts 403, so the policy layer refuses before the handler ever reads the body; the value only has to be well-formed and traceable to this note.
variables._upstream_charge_id_note: The payment half of the same key. Same reasoning as upstream_deal_id and one step further: sdk-payment exposes charge, refund, distribute, methods and provider but no charge READ, so not only does LeadFlow not create charges, it cannot look one up either - which is why the saga verifies payment from the evidence the caller presents rather than by reading it back.

dev._status: Host-run tools: localhost. The containerised Test MCP runner CANNOT reach these — use environment 'dev_container' for that, which is the same servers under host.docker.internal. discovered from client/vite.config.ts server.port=5173 and server/.env.example PORT=3010. baseUrl is the UI origin (5173) because the UI runner drives a browser against it; apiUrl is the Express origin (3010) that the api_definition runner calls. Pointing baseUrl at 3010 makes every UI step land on the JSON API and 404.

variables._test_password_note: Shared by the register and login api_definitions. A password is never returned in a response, so login cannot capture it from register and both must reference this one value. Declared per environment, not globally: a password is secret-shaped, and a global would apply this dev value to every environment.
variables._absent_outbox_delivery_id_note: A well-formed UUID that deliberately matches NO parked outbox row, for the 404 case on POST /api/leadflow/events/outbox/{id}/replay. Declared as a variable rather than {{dynamic:uuid}} because MUST-36 bans a generated id in a foreign-key position, and rightly: a random id in a path is indistinguishable from a producer that was never wired. There is no producer here by design - a dead-letter row cannot be created through the API, only reached by exhausting retries - so the no-producer form is the correct one.

dev_container._status: FOR THE CONTAINERISED TEST MCP RUNNER. Same machine and same servers as 'dev' — only the hostname differs, and it has to. Verified on this machine: from INSIDE projexlight-test-mcp, host.docker.internal:5173 and :3010 both answer 200 while localhost does not resolve to the host at all; from the HOST the reverse is true, host.docker.internal does not resolve. The two are mutually exclusive, which is why this is a separate environment rather than an edit to 'dev' — changing 'dev' would fix the container runner and break every host-run tool.
dev_container._port_note: 5173 is the Vite app and 3010 is the Express API — NOT 3000/5000. Port 3000 on this machine serves ProjexCloud's Next.js app and answers 200, so pointing the UI runner there does not fail fast: it loads someone else's application and every step fails with a confusing 'element not found'. Port 5000 is not listening at all. Confirmed by title: :3000 is 'ProjexCloud', :5173 is 'LeadFlow — The AI Revenue Operating System'.

development._status: Written by mcp-server/run-all-tests.sh port auto-detection, which always targets the key 'development' regardless of activeEnvironment, and which the UI runner then resolves against. It therefore needs the SAME portal names and variables as 'dev' (MUST-57) or every @portal:leadflow scenario aborts with 'portal not defined'. Same local hosts as dev on purpose - both describe this machine.

variables._test_password_note: Mirrors environments.dev.variables. Both keys describe this same local machine, so the dev password is correct here; it is still declared per environment rather than globally so it can never reach qa, staging or production.

leadflow._status: Local auth adapter. ProjexCloud becomes the identity authority when the identity spine lands; the realm name, the routes and the token shape do not change. Field names read from client/src/pages/auth/SignIn.tsx and SignUp.tsx.

default._status: Dev-only account for the BDD runner. Left empty previously on the assumption that canSelfRegister:true would make the runner self-register and cache the result — it does not for the UI runner, which substitutes ${login:email}/${login:password} straight from here. Empty strings therefore typed nothing into the sign-in form and EVERY auth-gated scenario failed with 'Password is required.' rather than a LOGIN_FAILED that would have named the cause. The Dev MCP registers this account automatically if it is absent from the database, so a fresh environment needs no manual step.
default._scope: dev only. The .test TLD is reserved by RFC 2606 and can never be a real mailbox, so this address cannot receive mail or collide with a customer. Do NOT copy these values into qa/staging/production — provision those out of band and pass them with run-all-tests.sh --login-email/--login-password.
default._role_requirement: MUST HOLD users.role='admin' IN ANY ENVIRONMENT THE API SUITE RUNS AGAINST. The mutating routing and SLA endpoints sit behind the policy decision point. The local role bridge maps 'user' -> sales_rep, and a Sales Rep correctly holds none of routing.configure, lead.reassign, sla.configure, sla.evaluate or sla.alert_dispatch — so an unelevated account makes 7 endpoints answer 403 and leaves 4 more skipped, because the PATCH/DELETE definitions need an id captured from a POST that never succeeded. 'admin' maps to revenue_operations + sales_manager, which covers all five. In dev this is applied automatically at boot by server/src/db/devSeed.ts (DEV_ADMIN_EMAIL / DEV_ADMIN_PASSWORD must match the values here). That seed REFUSES to run when NODE_ENV=production, so on any deployed target the role has to be granted out of band — see ProjexCloud docs/prod-setup/qa-fixture-seeds.md.

admin._status: Same account as `default`, exposed under the role name so the Dev MCP can pre-fetch an ADMIN token. Its _prefetch_role_tokens reads testCredentials.<role> for every role any definition declares in requiresRole, and warns 'no testCredentials.admin configured — those endpoints will 403' when the key is absent. That was the state until now: the account existed and held admin, but nothing pointed the runner at it.
admin._why_not_the_default_token: Definitions authenticate with {{cache:auth.login.response.data.token}}, and login dependsOn register — so the default token belongs to a freshly registered throwaway user, which the role bridge maps to sales_rep. The admin-scoped endpoints therefore answered 403 even though this admin account was configured and working the whole time.

data_steward._status: Seeded idempotently at boot by server/src/db/devSeed.ts (DEV_STEWARD_EMAIL / DEV_STEWARD_PASSWORD must match these values). A SEPARATE account from `admin` on purpose: users.role holds one value, and config/policies.ts grants the capture-resolution actions to data_steward alone.
data_steward._role_requirement: MUST HOLD users.role='steward', which LOCAL_ROLE_BRIDGE maps to the data_steward SOP role. An admin caller is NOT a substitute — admin bridges to revenue_operations + sales_manager + sales_rep, none of which holds these grants, which is why every capture-resolve dataset answered 403.
